title: ResolvedSessionConfig
description: The output of layered resolution (defaults, tenant, profile, session overrides, then language/channel/role overlays). Resolved once in the control plane, hashed, stored with the session and handed to the worker as a finished document. This is one of exactly two contact points between the Go and Python halves of the platform.

configHash.description: Hex SHA-256 over the canonical serialization of this document with configHash itself omitted. Makes any session explainable and replayable.

privacyMode.description: An agent that transcribes or responds must decrypt the audio, so end-to-end encryption and AI participation are mutually exclusive unless the agent holds a key. Enforced at the control plane, not by convention.

residency.description: Providers and storage are filtered to allowed regions at resolution time; a violation is an error now, not at first use.

pool.description: The worker pool this session dispatches to, addressed by name over the media server's own protocol. A config field rather than a constant, so a second pool can serve one language or tenant without a rewrite.

mode.description: Cascaded is the default. Half-cascade and speech-to-speech are provider modes, and switching is a config edit.

personaRef.description: Reference to a prompt/persona document. Never inline prose.

ProviderRef.description: Providers are named by variable and pinned by model version, so a vendor silently upgrading a model cannot silently change a consumer's agent.

Pipeline.description: Stage assembly. With a realtime provider the stt/llm/tts stages collapse and the rest is unchanged.

Turn.description: Every bad voice demo fails here, not on the LLM. Semantic turn detectors are English-trained and degrade elsewhere, which is why strategy resolves per language rather than globally.

localVadEnabled.description: Turn off where a provider's server VAD is authoritative: a second local VAD sees the same audio as the recognizer and fights it.

layout.description: A track egress attaches to a published track and cannot start before the participant publishes, so no-gap coverage requires room_composite started at session creation.

consentArtifactId.description: Recording and storage cannot proceed without a valid artifact. Consent is a gate in the control plane, not a flag a consumer can forget to check.

Budgets.description: Budgets live in config so violations alert automatically instead of regressing silently.
